note: Sign positions measured Day 14, 26 Aug, by clicking the FLOOR at the base of the wall each sign is mounted on, in an undistorted clip1 frame, converted through homography_camC.npz. Five clicks along the sign wall agreed on y to within 1 cm (1.64-1.65 m), so the y figure is a measurement, not a single reading. Hardcoded rather than OCR'd: signage OCR was cut on Day 12 and the sign text was known in advance, so only the reading is manual - the audit is unaffected.

junction.note: Three openings, measured Day 14 by clicking the floor at the mouth of each in an undistorted clip13 frame. Independent of any detector output: measured from the building, not from the data. Used as the pipeline sanity check - if the biggest hotspot did not land near the junction, something upstream would be wrong.

signs.text_note: THREE SEPARATE A5 SHEETS, not one board: GATES A-C, BAGGAGE CLAIM, EXIT, stacked vertically flush with no gaps, all at the same height on the same wall. Corrected Day 16 - Day 14 and Day 15 both described this as a single sign, and commit 297ede4 says Same board, which is wrong. The floor position is unaffected: the sheets share one wall and one footprint, so the Day 14 measurement (five clicks agreeing on y to within 1 cm) still stands and nothing was re-measured. Modelled as one entry rather than three because three identical coordinates would make nearest_sign arbitrary - hotspots.py uses a strict dist < best_d, so sheets two and three could never win and would be invisible in the output.
signs.absent_note: TOILETS and LOUNGE were deliberately omitted at shoot time to generate genuine wayfinding uncertainty. Trips categorised MISSING are those whose destination is absent from EVERY SIGN AT THIS JUNCTION. Three separate signs are posted here - GATES A-C, BAGGAGE CLAIM, EXIT - and neither TOILETS nor LOUNGE appears on any of them. Three chances to be signposted, three misses. This is a signage GAP, not a sparse sign: the corridor IS signposted, just not for where these people were going.
